claims.text: R4 table-driven cases, one table per list, each asserting category and the recorded rule_id; every v2 rule is exercised.
Precedence (override > protected > profile > firm > table > default) tested with each line's rule id.

Failure modes / idempotency: re-categorising a statement under v2 with overrides, profile and firm rules gives identical category, rule_id and reversal on every line (test_categorise_is_idempotent_under_v2_with_every_source, contracts). External calls: not applicable, the categoriser makes none. Retries/dead letter: not applicable, no queue.

Data/migration: additive (new v2.yaml, optional Transaction.rule_id, new evidence key 'lines'); old evidence keys kept (test_cma_run_under_v1_records_v1_rule_ids_and_keeps_old_evidence_keys). Reversible: switching a v2-categorised statement back to v1 equals a fresh v1 run, no repair (test_rollback_to_v1_after_v2_restores_v1_categories_and_rule_ids, dual_run). Backfill: not applicable, no stored data. P7: M1-M16 unchanged on the whole committed corpus under v2 and only the listed lines change category.
PII: the evidence 'lines' entries carry exactly id, category, rule_id and reverses, never descriptions (test_evidence_lines_carry_ids_only_never_descriptions, contracts).

Security: no new entry point (CMA_RULESET already exists; an unknown id is refused with exit 2, tests/test_cli.py). Input validation at the boundary: malformed v2 rules (names, unless, protected, ordering) refused naming the problem. No secrets; no new dependency (yaml, re, pydantic already used).
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q tests/test_cli.py; python -m pytest -q tests/test_rules_v2.py -k malformed

claims.text: Performance: categorising 10,000 lines under v2 with a profile is under the 2 s recompute target (measured about 0.16 s; test bound 2 s). No queries or list endpoints: not applicable.

Observability: the evidence file proves the behaviour ran, recording ruleset id and hash and each line's rule id (test_cma_run_under_v2_categorises_with_v2_and_records_each_lines_rule). Alerts/dashboards: not applicable by design (local tool, no remote alerting); the failure that matters, a bad table, is a refusal at load.
Operability: behind CMA_RULESET (default v1); rollback is CMA_RULESET=v1, exercised by the dual_run rollback test. No config or secrets changes for deploy.

Docs: README updated for v2 (lists, cash counted as trading, per-line rule ids in evidence, v1 rollback) and the categoriser row now states the precedence. Design decision is already in design.md (rule tables as data sub-decision).
